test_title: PYST 17: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 14 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following infrastructure initiatives is associated with urban development in India?

options.text: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan
Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation

solution:
The correct answer is __**Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)** was launched on **25th June 2015** by the Government of India. Its main aim is to improve urban infrastructure to ensure better living conditions in cities.
 
• The mission focuses on providing basic civic amenities like **water supply, sewerage, urban transport, and parks** for better quality of life and robust infrastructure development in cities.
 
• AMRUT covers **500 cities** across India with a population of over **one lakh**, including cities in hilly areas, islands, and tourist destinations. 
 
• The mission adopts a bottom-up planning approach where urban local bodies (ULBs) prepare Service Level Improvement Plans (SLIPs) for infrastructure development based on their local needs.
 
• The primary components of AMRUT include ensuring **universal coverage of water supply, improved sanitation facilities, stormwater drainage, and reduction in pollution levels** by promoting non-motorized transport. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **RURBAN Mission:**

 
 
• Launched in **2016** under the Ministry of Rural Development, the mission focuses on developing **rural clusters** by providing urban-like amenities while retaining the rural essence.
 
• The mission aims to bridge the rural-urban divide by creating **economic, social, and infrastructure facilities** in rural areas. 
 
• Its objective is to develop **smart villages** with access to healthcare, education, skill development, sanitation, and housing facilities.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM):**
 
 
• Launched in **2019**, PM-KUSUM primarily focuses on providing **solar energy** solutions to farmers.
 
• The scheme aims to install **solar pumps, grid-connected solar power plants**, and solarization of existing pumps to promote renewable energy and reduce dependency on conventional power sources.
 
• It is not directly related to urban development but focuses on improving energy access and agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Managed Services Provider Scheme:**
 
 
• This scheme is **not associated with urban development**. It primarily focuses on providing managed IT and digital services to businesses and government organizations.
 
• It is a technical initiative aimed at enhancing digital transformation rather than addressing urban infrastructure needs.
 
 
 
• **AMRUT Scheme Features:**
 
 
• AMRUT encourages states to adopt reforms in governance, such as promoting **online services, GIS-based planning, and energy efficiency**.
 
• It emphasizes capacity building for urban local bodies (ULBs) and training personnel to manage urban infrastructure projects effectively.
 
• The funding pattern under AMRUT is shared between the central and state governments, with a **central assistance of 50%** for cities with a population of less than 10 lakh.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Urbanization in India:**

 
 
• India is experiencing rapid urbanization, with over **35% of its population** living in urban areas as per the **2011 Census**. This number is expected to increase to over **50% by 2050**.
 
• Urban development initiatives like AMRUT aim to address challenges like **population density, environmental sustainability, and infrastructure deficits**.
 
• Efforts such as smart cities, metro rail projects, and housing for all contribute to urban transformation in India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of AMRUT:**
 
 
• It complements other urban development schemes such as **Smart Cities Mission** and **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, creating a holistic approach to urban infrastructure improvement.
 
• By focusing on **basic amenities**, AMRUT ensures inclusivity and sustainability in urban planning.
 
• Its emphasis on **citizen-centric governance** promotes transparency, accountability, and active participation in urban development projects.
